title: A jobs miss, a firm dollar, and miners that bought the dip
paragraphs: Friday should have been a good day for gold. US payrolls rose by only 29,000 against 90,000 expected, unemployment ticked up to 4.2% and the market's odds of a Fed hike in October fell from 28% to 15%. Instead the dollar index held near the top of its range at 101.93, and gold spot slipped 0.8% to $4,143. That is the divergence the Dollar Balance has been tracking: weak data, no relief.

The ratios took it calmly. Gold/silver moved from 68.85 on Wednesday to 68.62 on Friday. Over the three days silver held its ground, flat while gold slipped 0.4%; on Friday itself silver fell 1.0% against gold's 0.8%, a hair more, not a rout. There was no flight out of silver, even with Shanghai closed for Golden Week and no Chinese physical buying all week.

The miners did the opposite of a warning. On Friday GDX rose 1.2% while GLD fell 0.7%, lifting miners/gold from 0.2266 to 0.2309. One plausible reason sits on the crack spreads page: diesel futures fell about 4% since Wednesday, and diesel is one of a miner's largest running costs. Juniors/majors eased from 1.298 to 1.295, a drift, not a turn.

What to watch: Shanghai reopens on Thursday 8 October with a week of price moves to catch up on. Then US CPI on Wednesday 14 October. On the last inflation day, 30 September, the gold/silver ratio rose and silver broke below its 61.0 support; the CPI reading will show whether silver repeats that or holds this time.
